disposition: FIXED IN THE ENGINE -- implemented, verified on all three shapes, committed
engine_commit: 51fb18a1 fix(engine): route a conflict by its shape, not by one answer for all

why_the_hold_off_was_lifted.the_original_reason: the engine repo has ~1780 dirty tracked files and another live session's uncommitted work; a commit there would sweep that work in
why_the_hold_off_was_lifted.what_changed: the dirty set was re-measured, not assumed: 1787 dirty paths, of which 1735 are .saipen/ and the rest are saipen/*.md docs, tools/run_scenarios.py, ruff.toml, VERSION, README.md
why_the_hold_off_was_lifted.the_decisive_fact: tools/saipen.py and tools/saipen_engine/journal.py were CLEAN -- neither appears in git status for those paths
why_the_hold_off_was_lifted.consequence: the commit was path-limited to tools/saipen_engine/journal.py. The resulting commit contains exactly one file. No other session's work was included, and none of it was modified.
why_the_hold_off_was_lifted.the_engine_pre_commit_gate: the engine's own tools/validate.py ran as a pre-commit hook and reported conformance clean with 34 warnings and 0 problems

the_fix.shape_of_the_change: recovery_preflight's CONFLICT refusal now chooses canonical_next_command by the conflict's shape instead of emitting one answer for every CONFLICT
the_fix.the_predicate: _conflict_diverges(root, op_id) delegates to inspect_op -- the same read-only probe the message already tells the operator to run -- and returns True when it reports conflicting_locations
the_fix.why_delegate_rather_than_re_derive: a second copy of the settle path's judgement would drift from the first. The first attempt re-implemented the classification from the plan's before/after hashes and was WRONG: it reported the non-prefix-materialization fixture as non-divergent and would have named `saipen recover` for an op that bare recover refuses. inspect_op is the surface that already makes this judgement, and it is the same probe the operator runs, so advice and diagnostic cannot disagree.
the_fix.fails_closed: an op that will not inspect returns True, so unreadable recovery evidence keeps routing to the explicit resolution classes exactly as before
the_fix.new_field: conflict_diverged: bool on the RECOVERY_CONFLICT answer, so a caller can branch on the shape without re-deriving it
the_fix.what_did_not_change: the CONFLICT status, recovery_required: True, the refusal itself, inspect_command, and every safety property. The divergent shape still refuses; nothing that previously refused now proceeds.

All five checks pass: DIVERGENT_SHAPE_STILL_PROTECTED
verification_on_every_shape.why_a_new_probe_was_needed: T-1400's harness puts its divergence in .saipen/LOG.md as a non-grammar line, so the immutable-ledger validator rejects the tree with HISTORY_LEDGER_CORRUPT before recovery is reached. It proves bare recover refuses; it cannot exercise the routing my fix changed. This probe diverges BOARD.md instead and reaches preflight.
verification_on_every_shape.the_four_discarded_injection_attempts: appending a new ticket line (CORE-003, no allocation event), injecting into DOING (ACTIVE_TICKET_MISMATCH, DOING is the active slot), injecting into TODO (CORE-003 again), and appending text after the fields (INVALID claim, because the append landed inside claim_time). One lesson four times: an injection into a validated file must be a VALID change, or the validator answers instead of the probe. The harness docstring records this rather than presenting a first-try success.
verification_on_every_shape.why_this_matters: this is the shape T-1355 measured and its fix protects. Naming bare recover for THIS shape would have recreated the loop T-1355 removed. It is not named for it, and that is now measured rather than asserted.
